Composition

How GIFTs connect

Shared output and input anchors create directed edges. Internal metabolites never create implicit links.

Each edge is one declared anchor shared by an upstream output boundary and a downstream input boundary.

Anchors are drawn once. An anchor with an incoming and an outgoing edge is the exact boundary where two GIFTs compose.

Change history 2 entries

  1. 2026.08.22026-08-1717:45 UTCnone
    Marker layer audited against KEGG orthology; no orthologs missing
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Confirm whether other genomic markers are acceptable for the curated enzymes before broadening the evidence layer, and record the rejected candidates so they are not re-proposed.
    Evidence
    The accepted markers of all 27 reactions were compared against every KO that KEGG assigns to the corresponding EC number, and against the step logic of modules M00048-M00052. Twenty-six of 27 reactions matched exactly; the only difference was the regulatory K00610 retired in this release.
    Effect
    No markers added. K06863 stays off the folate-dependent AICAR transformylase because purP is formate-dependent and modelled as RHEA:24836. K01948 (EC 6.3.4.16) remains unacceptable for the glutamine-dependent RHEA:18633. Non-KO namespaces validate and resolve correctly but were not adopted, because evaluation has no confidence filter and weaker evidence would silently change calls.
  2. 2026.08.12026-08-17none
    Initial curated release of five nucleotide biosynthesis GIFTs
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Establish the reference content of giftr as biologically bounded capabilities between declared molecular anchors, derived from but not equal to KEGG modules M00048 to M00052.
    Evidence
    Rhea release 141 reaction chemistry, ChEBI release 253 anchor identity, KEGG modules M00048-M00052 for pathway organisation and orthology assignment.
    Effect
    Baseline release. Purine core, adenylate, guanylate, pyrimidine core and cytidylate biosynthesis become callable, composing through the shared IMP anchor.
Curator noteAtomic branch derived from KEGG M00049; ends at AMP because shared nucleotide phosphorylation is intentionally excluded.

Change history 3 entries

  1. 2026.09.42026-08-1814:00 UTCnone
    The pentose anchors use the generic sugar rather than a single anomer
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Rhea represents ABC import of the generic sugar and uses one ChEBI identifier for both sides of the membrane. The anomer-specific identities previously recorded described the isomerase substrate rather than the boundary molecule, and would have made the transport and catabolic reactions appear to act on different substances.
    Evidence
    Rhea RHEA:29899 and RHEA:30007 use CHEBI:53455 and CHEBI:17535 for both the external and internal participant.
    Effect
    No call changes; no route reaction was altered.
  2. 2026.09.42026-08-1814:00 UTCbroadens
    D-xylose and L-arabinose uptake curated, and their anchors split by compartment
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Import is what separates a genome that can use a sugar released by others from one that merely encodes the catabolic enzymes, and it is the first place the compartment layer carries real content. Both pentoses have substrate-specific ABC importer orthologues and a Rhea master for the translocation, so both conditions of the splitting licence are met.
    Evidence
    KEGG orthology K10543/K10544/K10545, K10537/K10538/K10539 and K25045/K25046/K25047; Rhea master reactions RHEA:29899 and RHEA:30007, both carrying explicit (out) and (in) participants.
    Effect
    Two new positive calls become possible, and the first composition edges in the catabolic half of the database appear: uptake now feeds the matching degradation GIFT through the cytoplasmic anchor.
  3. 2026.09.32026-08-1810:00 UTCbroadens
    Nine monosaccharide and uronate degradation GIFTs added as the first catabolic content
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Monosaccharide catabolism is the tier that connects carbohydrate degradation to central metabolism, and it is the half of the degradation model that needs no polymer chemistry. Each GIFT ends at the central metabolite the sugar actually becomes, so capabilities that yield different products are separate traits rather than routes of one trait.
    Evidence
    Rhea release 141 master reactions and KEGG orthology, every accession verified against the resource on 2026-08-18. KEGG modules M00632 and M00061 match two of the nine boundaries exactly; the other seven have no module.
    Effect
    Nine new positive calls become possible. No existing GIFT call changes; the new content shares no reaction with the biosynthetic GIFTs.
Curator noteConvergence on D-xylulose 5-phosphate is why arabinofuranosidase side-chain release composes with this GIFT rather than needing its own downstream chemistry.

    Marker policy prefers a subfamily over a polyspecific family, but the family-level substrate mapping shipped by dbCAN contains no subfamily rows, so the first polysaccharide release accepted bare families and recorded them as ambiguous. The subfamily assignments live in the dbCAN-sub HMM library, whose profile names encode the eCAMI cluster, its parent family, the official CAZy subfamilies it contains, and the EC numbers its members carry, each with a member count. Streaming the library and keeping only those names yields a 104 KB table from a 4.9 GB artifact. Confidence now comes from two measured quantities rather than one: how dominant an EC is among the EC-annotated members of a cluster, and how many members support it. Clusters whose parent family belongs to a different catalytic class are excluded, and carbohydrate-binding modules are excluded entirely because they catalyse nothing.
    Evidence
    dbCAN-sub HMM library db_v5-2-9_5-5-2026, 53411 profiles, of which 2474 carry at least one EC assignment; derived table in data-raw/reference/cazy-subfamily-ec.tsv with the extraction script alongside it.
    Effect
    267 subfamily evidence rows added across seven catalytic components. Genomes annotated by dbCAN-sub gain calls they previously missed, and a call resting on a specific subfamily now reports curated or high-confidence where a bare family reported ambiguous. Bare families are retained as a lower-confidence fallback, so no genome loses a call.
  2. 2026.11.12026-08-1823:59 UTCnone
    GIFTs and anchors carry a registered facet vocabulary, and a derived profile is exposed alongside it
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    A single free-text category could not answer questions that cut across it, and the information needed to answer them was already present in the declared anchors and the compartment layer with no way out. The facet vocabulary is registered so that a multi-valued classification cannot degenerate into free text: substrate_class is single-valued and therefore partitions the database, while physiological_role and the anchor facets are multi-valued and return supersets. Nothing in the derived profile is curated, and neither facets nor profile enter the completeness logic that produces a call.
    Evidence
    Declared anchors, anchor compartment, and the anchor-derived composition graph, all already present in the database.
    Effect
    No call changes. The former gift.category column is replaced by the substrate_class facet.
  3. 2026.10.22026-08-1821:00 UTCmixed
    Polysaccharide degradation is curated per substrate capability rather than per enzymatic step
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The first polysaccharide release split each substrate into single-reaction GIFTs for endo-acting depolymerisation, exo-acting saccharification and debranching. That made a GIFT equivalent to a reaction, which is the marker-checklist shape the ontology exists to avoid, and it left the question a user actually asks - can this genome degrade xylan - unanswerable by any single trait. The separation was motivated by the primary-degrader versus cross-feeder distinction, which is real, but that distinction is already carried by the incomplete-route diagnostics: a genome with only the endo-acting enzyme is now reported as incomplete with the exo-acting reaction named as missing, which is more informative than a separate positive trait because it says what is absent. Oligosaccharide intermediates return to being internal; they would be promoted back to anchors only if an oligosaccharide importer could be evidenced, which would make selfish foraging an independently meaningful capability.
    Evidence
    giftr evaluation contract: route completeness with closest-route and missing-reaction reporting. Invariant 9 of AGENTS.md, which forbids both arbitrary single-step fragments and bundles of independently meaningful capabilities.
    Effect
    Six single-reaction GIFTs are replaced by three substrate-level capabilities. Genomes carrying a complete endo-plus-exo enzyme set keep a positive call; genomes carrying only one side of it now report an incomplete capability with the missing reaction named, where they previously reported a positive call for a fragment. Two anchors are withdrawn.
  4. 2026.10.12026-08-1818:00 UTCnone
    CAZy families accepted as markers, with confidence derived from measured family polyspecificity
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    A CAZy family is a sequence family, not an activity. Accepting a family as evidence for one of its activities silently attributes the others, so confidence is set from the number of distinct characterised activities the family carries in dbCAN: one activity is curated, two or three is high-confidence, four or more is ambiguous. GH5 carries 28 and GH13 carries 34, so neither is evidence for a specific chemistry on its own; GH52, GH120 and GH62 carry one each.
    Evidence
    Distinct EC counts computed directly from the pinned dbCAN mapping and recorded per marker in component_markers.notes.
    Effect
    Calls resting only on polyspecific families report evidence_confidence = ambiguous rather than reading like curated orthology.
  5. 2026.10.12026-08-1818:00 UTCnone
    A CAZy family and a KEGG orthologue are alternative markers of one catalytic role, not alternative enzyme systems
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The proposal suggested one enzyme system per non-homologous CAZy family. At implementation these are all single-protein hydrolases, and an annotation pipeline cannot tell whether the family hit and the orthology hit describe the same protein - they usually do. Modelling them as alternative systems would imply two enzymes where there is one. The system and component layers remain available for genuinely multi-subunit CAZyme architectures.
    Evidence
    Absence of subunit structure in the curated hydrolases; overlap between CAZy and KEGG annotation of the same protein.
    Effect
    No call changes; the Boolean result is identical either way.
  6. 2026.10.12026-08-1818:00 UTCbroadens
    Arabinoxylan and starch depolymerisation and saccharification curated as separate tiers
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Endo-acting depolymerisation and exo-acting saccharification are curated as separate GIFTs because possessing one without the other is the primary-degrader versus cross-feeder distinction, which is the main thing a carbohydrate database is asked to resolve. Polymer and oligosaccharide anchors are extracellular: a polymer cannot cross a membrane, and no oligosaccharide importer could be evidenced, so the products of their cleavage are outside the cell. Side-chain release earns its own GIFT because the released L-arabinose is itself an anchored fermentable sugar.
    Evidence
    CAZy family and activity assignments from dbCAN db_v5-2-9_5-5-2026 fam-substrate-mapping.tsv; KEGG orthology entries verified 2026-08-18. None of the six EC numbers has a Rhea master reaction.
    Effect
    Six new positive calls become possible, and the first complete traversal from a dietary polysaccharide to central metabolism appears in the derived graph.
Curator noteKept separate from xylan degradation because L-arabinose is itself an anchored fermentable sugar, so the same arabinose GIFTs serve arabinoxylan, arabinan and arabinogalactan without triplicate curation. One reaction, but a complete capability with its own product.
GIFT 05

Aspartate chemoreception

aspartate_chemoreception
regulatory—curatedv1

Encodes the machinery to detect L-aspartate and transduce it into the chemotaxis pathway: the Tar aspartate chemoreceptor together with the shared chemotaxis kinase, response-regulator and adaptation functions. A positive call means the genome encodes an aspartate-responsive chemosensory input. It does not mean the cell swims toward aspartate, which additionally requires expression, a working flagellar motor, and a gradient.

    Regulatory specificity cannot exceed evidence specificity. The generic chemoreceptor accession K03406 is deliberately refused here: it identifies the conserved cytoplasmic signalling domain shared by every chemoreceptor and cannot single out an aspartate sensor, so accepting it would let any chemotactic genome claim aspartate sensing.     Nine serine, glycine, aspartate-family, cysteine and methionine biosynthesis GIFTs added
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Extend giftr beyond nucleotide metabolism with the amino acid capabilities most often needed to interpret host-associated genomes, curated as bounded capabilities rather than as imported KEGG modules.
    Evidence
    KEGG modules M00016-M00021, M00338 and M00609 for orthology and pathway organisation; Rhea release 141 for reaction identity, direction and ChEBI participants; KEGG gene-to-organism links for the prevalence figures quoted in the accompanying change entries.
    Effect
    Eleven anchors, nine GIFTs, nineteen routes and twenty-five reactions become callable. The amino acid GIFTs compose into a single acyclic chain from 3-phosphoglycerate through serine and cysteine to methionine, and from aspartate through the semialdehyde and homoserine branchpoints to threonine and methionine.
  2. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCnone
    The aspartate-to-homoserine trunk is curated once instead of twice
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    KEGG M00018 and M00017 both contain aspartate kinase, aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase and homoserine dehydrogenase. Importing both modules as GIFTs would encode the same three reactions twice and let the two copies drift apart. The trunk is cut at the two real branchpoints instead.
    Evidence
    6569 KEGG organisms satisfy the orthology of both modules, so the duplication would be exercised in the majority of genomes carrying either. L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde is the branchpoint to lysine and diaminopimelate (M00016); L-homoserine is the branchpoint to threonine and methionine and is named in both module titles.
    Effect
    aspartate_semialdehyde_biosynthesis and homoserine_biosynthesis carry the shared chemistry; threonine and methionine biosynthesis begin at the homoserine anchor and compose through it. The lysine and diaminopimelate branch can later attach at the semialdehyde anchor without re-cutting any existing GIFT.
Curator noteShared head of KEGG M00018 and M00017, cut out so that neither module duplicates it. Anchored at the semialdehyde so the lysine and diaminopimelate branch can attach without re-cutting this GIFT.
GIFT 07

Chemotaxis signal transduction

chemotaxis_signal_transduction
regulatory—curatedv1

Encodes the core chemotaxis signal-transduction machinery: a chemoreceptor, the CheA histidine kinase with its CheW coupling protein, the CheY response regulator, and the CheR/CheB adaptation cycle. A positive call means the genome encodes that pathway. It does not mean the cell is chemotactic, that the pathway is expressed, or that the organism responds to any particular compound: which chemoeffectors are detected depends on receptor sensing domains this claim says nothing about.

    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The chemotaxis pathway is the clearest case of a capability that is neither chemistry nor a structure: it is an information-transduction circuit, complete when a receptor, a kinase core, a response regulator and an adaptation cycle are jointly encoded. It was curated first because it needs no evidence the marker model lacks.
    Evidence
    KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18: K03406, K03407, K03408, K00575, K03412, K03413 and the termination phosphatases K03414, K03410, K03409. Receptor distribution was measured rather than assumed: Escherichia coli K-12 carries no K03406 orthologue, its four receptors being assigned to the characterised groups K05874, K05875, K05876 and K03776, while Pseudomonas aeruginosa carries 21 K03406 genes and Vibrio cholerae 34.
    Effect
    chemotaxis_signal_transduction becomes callable through CIRCUIT_CHEMOTAXIS_CORE with four required functions. The reception function accepts a generic or a characterised chemoreceptor, so an Escherichia coli annotation is not called receptor-less. Signal termination is accessory with three non-homologous systems.
Curator noteThe reception function accepts either a generic methyl-accepting chemotaxis protein (K03406) or any characterised chemoreceptor. Both are needed: Escherichia coli K-12 carries no K03406 orthologue at all, its four receptors being assigned to the characterised groups, while Pseudomonas aeruginosa carries 21 K03406 genes and Vibrio cholerae 34. Signal termination is accessory and has three non-homologous implementations (CheZ, CheC, CheX). CheV is not accepted as a CheW substitute. See inst/doc/proposal-regulatory-gifts.md.

  1. 2026.12.12026-08-1812:00 UTCbroadens
    Collagen cleavage curated as the first protein-degradation GIFT, with a protein substrate class and a host tissue degradation role
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Protein degradation was proposed as a layer of eight substrate-specific traits. Applying the evidence test of the polysaccharide proposal to real markers licensed one. Collagen passes on mechanism rather than on nomenclature: EC 3.4.24.3 is defined by digestion of native collagen in the triple-helical region, an activity generic endopeptidases lack because the intact helix resists them, and KEGG assigns K01387 to MEROPS family M9 and to extracellular-matrix-damaging toxins while keeping the host collagenases MMP-1 and MMP-8 as separate orthologues. The trait therefore claims no more than its markers support. The product is anchored as collagen peptides rather than as a shared peptide pool, because a pool has no membership criterion and would connect every protein-degradation GIFT to every other one's downstream through an undefined intermediate; a shared oligopeptide tier is deferred behind peptide transporter evidence, on the same licence that keeps oligosaccharides internal. The capability needed no schema change: anchors were never restricted to small molecules, rhea_master has been nullable since schema 4, and the marker namespace vocabulary is open.
    Evidence
    KEGG orthology K01387 and EC 3.4.24.3, verified 2026-08-18; Pfam PF01752 via InterPro, retrieved 2026-08-18; Rhea searched 2026-08-18 and found to contain collagen hydroxylation, glycosylation and crosslinking but no proteolytic cleavage of the helix. Full assessment in inst/doc/proposal-protein-degradation.md.
    Effect
    One GIFT, two anchors, one reaction, one route, one enzyme system, one component and two marker evidence rows are added. Genomes encoding a family M9 collagenase gain a positive call. Four facet terms are registered and two anchor facet definitions are broadened from glycan-only wording to cover proteins; no existing anchor is reclassified and no existing call changes.
  2. 2026.12.12026-08-1812:00 UTCnone
    Trait specificity may not exceed marker specificity, and seven candidate protein-degradation traits are refused under that rule
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The rule was already enforced for carbohydrate-active enzymes as marker policy, where accepting a polyspecific family such as GH5 for a cellulose component would make every mannan degrader a cellulose degrader. Stated as marker policy it reads as advice about confidence values; it is in fact a constraint on what a GIFT may be called, so it is promoted to a named invariant. The protein layer makes the constraint concrete. Elastin cleavage was refused although a named orthologue exists, because EC 3.4.24.26 defines pseudolysin as hydrolysing elastin, collagen types III and IV, fibronectin and immunoglobulin A: accepting it would attribute an elastin-specific claim to a broadly proteolytic enzyme, and would equally license a collagen call, silently equating the two traits. That is the first recorded case of an over-broad marker damaging a trait other than the one it was accepted for. Keratin cleavage was refused for want of any orthologue, keratinolysis being an assay phenotype of subtilisins rather than a clade. Albumin, actin, glutelin, tropomyosin and troponin cleavage were refused because no microbial protease orthologue exists for them; searching for those substrates returns the host structural proteins themselves.
    Evidence
    KEGG orthology and enzyme records searched 2026-08-18 for each candidate substrate. Reasoning and per-substrate outcomes in inst/doc/proposal-protein-degradation.md, section 4.
    Effect
    No call changes. Seven candidate traits are refused rather than deferred silently, so the reasons are available when the evidence changes. AGENTS.md gains invariant 16.
Curator noteOne required reaction, but a complete capability with its own product, as for arabinoxylan debranching. Substrate specificity rests on mechanism rather than on a family name: EC 3.4.24.3 is defined by digestion of native collagen in the triple-helical region, which generic endopeptidases cannot perform because the intact helix resists them. Broadly proteolytic enzymes such as pseudolysin are deliberately excluded even though they hydrolyse collagen among other host proteins, because accepting them would equate this trait with generic proteolysis. The product anchor is substrate-specific rather than a shared peptide pool; a shared oligopeptide tier and peptide uptake are deferred behind transporter evidence.

Change history 3 entries

  1. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCbroadens
    Nine serine, glycine, aspartate-family, cysteine and methionine biosynthesis GIFTs added
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Extend giftr beyond nucleotide metabolism with the amino acid capabilities most often needed to interpret host-associated genomes, curated as bounded capabilities rather than as imported KEGG modules.
    Evidence
    KEGG modules M00016-M00021, M00338 and M00609 for orthology and pathway organisation; Rhea release 141 for reaction identity, direction and ChEBI participants; KEGG gene-to-organism links for the prevalence figures quoted in the accompanying change entries.
    Effect
    Eleven anchors, nine GIFTs, nineteen routes and twenty-five reactions become callable. The amino acid GIFTs compose into a single acyclic chain from 3-phosphoglycerate through serine and cysteine to methionine, and from aspartate through the semialdehyde and homoserine branchpoints to threonine and methionine.
  2. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCnone
    L-homocysteine is declared as an input anchor only, and methionine biosynthesis is not split at it
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Cysteine to methionine and homocysteine to cysteine is a real metabolic interconversion, so the obvious boundary choices make the anchor-derived composition graph cyclic and the database fails to build. Declaring homocysteine as an output anchor, or curating a methionine-to-homocysteine GIFT, re-creates the cycle.
    Evidence
    The source validator turns every output-anchor to input-anchor match into a directed edge and rejects cycles. With homocysteine as an output the graph closes through METHIONINE, HOMOCYSTEINE and CYSTEINE. In the organisms that use the mcc route the homocysteine consumed by cysteine biosynthesis comes from methionine salvage rather than from de novo methionine biosynthesis, so an input-only boundary is also the honest one.
    Effect
    L-homocysteine stays internal to both methionine GIFTs and is declared only as an input of cysteine_biosynthesis_homocysteine. Any future methionine salvage or SAM-cycle GIFT must revisit this boundary before it can be added.
  3. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCbroadens
    M00338 and the cysteine-forming tail of M00609 merged; the SAM-cycle steps of M00609 excluded
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The first four steps of M00609 are the activated methyl cycle, not cysteine biosynthesis. K17462 is a putative AdoMet-dependent methyltransferase with EC 2.1.1.- whose reaction R10404 has no Rhea master, and the SAM-to-SAH conversion it stands for is performed by hundreds of unrelated methyltransferases. Requiring it is a pathway-drawing convention, as K00610 was for aspartate carbamoyltransferase. The remaining two steps make cysteine from homocysteine, which is exactly what M00338 does by different chemistry.
    Evidence
    Of 489 KEGG organisms carrying both K17216 and K17217, only 332 carry K17462, so 157 would be called incomplete for a step that is not evidence of anything. None of the 2592 organisms carrying the M00338 pair K01697 and K01758 carries the M00609 pair, which makes the two enzyme sets taxonomically disjoint solutions to one problem rather than two traits.
    Effect
    cysteine_biosynthesis_homocysteine carries both chemistries as the alternative routes CYS_RT_SERINE and CYS_RT_OAS. The O-acetyl-L-serine route additionally requires serine O-acetyltransferase, which M00609 omits because its diagram enters at O-acetyl-L-serine; 486 of the 489 organisms carry it, so the added requirement costs almost no sensitivity.
Curator noteKEGG M00338 and the cysteine-forming tail of M00609 merged into one capability with two routes; their enzyme sets share no KEGG genome, which makes them alternatives rather than separate traits. The four SAM-cycle steps of M00609 are excluded.

Change history 2 entries

  1. 2026.08.22026-08-1717:45 UTCnone
    Marker layer audited against KEGG orthology; no orthologs missing
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Confirm whether other genomic markers are acceptable for the curated enzymes before broadening the evidence layer, and record the rejected candidates so they are not re-proposed.
    Evidence
    The accepted markers of all 27 reactions were compared against every KO that KEGG assigns to the corresponding EC number, and against the step logic of modules M00048-M00052. Twenty-six of 27 reactions matched exactly; the only difference was the regulatory K00610 retired in this release.
    Effect
    No markers added. K06863 stays off the folate-dependent AICAR transformylase because purP is formate-dependent and modelled as RHEA:24836. K01948 (EC 6.3.4.16) remains unacceptable for the glutamine-dependent RHEA:18633. Non-KO namespaces validate and resolve correctly but were not adopted, because evaluation has no confidence filter and weaker evidence would silently change calls.
  2. 2026.08.12026-08-17none
    Initial curated release of five nucleotide biosynthesis GIFTs
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Establish the reference content of giftr as biologically bounded capabilities between declared molecular anchors, derived from but not equal to KEGG modules M00048 to M00052.
    Evidence
    Rhea release 141 reaction chemistry, ChEBI release 253 anchor identity, KEGG modules M00048-M00052 for pathway organisation and orthology assignment.
    Effect
    Baseline release. Purine core, adenylate, guanylate, pyrimidine core and cytidylate biosynthesis become callable, composing through the shared IMP anchor.
Curator noteAtomic cytidylate-forming capability derived from KEGG M00052; shared UMP/UDP phosphorylation and CTP/CDP interconversion are intentionally excluded.
GIFT 12

Flagellar apparatus

flagellar_apparatus
structuralcell_surface_appendagecuratedv1

Encodes the structural and assembly machinery of a bacterial flagellum: the type III export apparatus, basal body, C ring, hook, filament and stator of at least one curated flagellar architecture. A positive call means the genome encodes that machinery. It does not mean the organism is motile, that the flagellum is expressed, or that it rotates under any particular condition.

Change history 2 entries

  1. 2026.12.22026-08-1809:25 UTCnone
    Proton- and sodium-driven flagellar apparatus refused at KO evidence level
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Naming a GIFT for its coupling ion would claim a specificity the evidence does not carry. The specificity of a GIFT claim must not exceed the specificity of the genomic evidence supporting it, and this is the structural instance of that invariant.
    Evidence
    KEGG assigns Vibrio cholerae PomA (VC_0892) and PomB (VC_0893), the sodium-driven polar flagellar stator, to K02556 and K02557, the same orthologues as the proton-driven MotA and MotB of Escherichia coli. MotX (K21217) and MotY (K21218) are specific to the sodium-type polar T ring but evidence a scaffold rather than an ion channel, and are absent from the sodium-driven MotPS motors of alkaliphilic Bacillus.
    Effect
    proton_driven_flagellar_apparatus and sodium_driven_flagellar_apparatus were not curated. The single flagellar_apparatus GIFT is deliberately silent about coupling ion, and the refusal is recorded in inst/doc/proposal-structural-gifts.md.
  2. 2026.12.22026-08-1809:20 UTCbroadens
    Flagellar apparatus added as the first structural GIFT
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The flagellum is the clearest case of a capability whose completeness is architectural rather than chemical: it is complete when a curated set of structural and assembly functions is jointly supported, and it has no meaningful input or output molecule. It exercises alternative architectures, multisubunit systems, a fused protein serving two components, and the evidence-specificity limit on ion coupling.
    Evidence
    KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18. Structural decomposition follows the export gate, basal body, C ring, hook, hook-filament junction, filament and stator of the characterised enterobacterial and Bacillus flagella; the L and P rings are curated as a separate diderm architecture because monoderms build a flagellum without them.
    Effect
    flagellar_apparatus becomes callable through two architectures, ARCH_FLAGELLUM_DIDERM and ARCH_FLAGELLUM_MONODERM, sharing nine structural functions. No metabolic call changed.
Curator noteIon coupling is deliberately not claimed. KEGG assigns the sodium-driven PomA/PomB stator of Vibrio cholerae to K02556/K02557, the same orthologues as the proton-driven MotA/MotB stator of Escherichia coli, so KO evidence cannot separate proton- from sodium-driven motors. Separate proton_driven_flagellar_apparatus and sodium_driven_flagellar_apparatus GIFTs are therefore refused at this evidence level; see inst/doc/proposal-structural-gifts.md. Transcriptional regulators (FlhDC, FliA, FlgM) are excluded because they are regulatory, not structural.

Change history 2 entries

  1. 2026.09.42026-08-1814:00 UTCnone
    Uptake GIFTs are curated only where transporter markers are substrate-specific and the translocation has a verified reaction identity
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Fucose, galactose and mannose are moved mainly by promiscuous carriers: the KEGG orthologue for fucose uptake is annotated as a fucose-galactose-glucose symporter, so accepting it would attribute fucose uptake to any genome carrying that family. Sialic acid, hexuronate and N-acetylglucosamine have substrate-specific markers but no reaction identity giftr can verify, because their symporters and importers carry no EC number and no Rhea master. In both cases no uptake GIFT is curated and the substrate anchor stays compartment-unspecified, so no catabolic chain is broken by a transporter that could not be evidenced.
    Evidence
    KEGG orthology entry K02429, annotated as an MFS fucose-galactose-glucose:H+ symporter; absence of an EC number or Rhea master for K03290 (nanT), K08191 (exuT) and K10200/K10201/K10202 (ngcEFG).
    Effect
    No call changes. Seven substrates keep an unspecified anchor and remain callable from their catabolic markers alone.
  2. 2026.09.32026-08-1810:00 UTCbroadens
    Nine monosaccharide and uronate degradation GIFTs added as the first catabolic content
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Monosaccharide catabolism is the tier that connects carbohydrate degradation to central metabolism, and it is the half of the degradation model that needs no polymer chemistry. Each GIFT ends at the central metabolite the sugar actually becomes, so capabilities that yield different products are separate traits rather than routes of one trait.
    Evidence
    Rhea release 141 master reactions and KEGG orthology, every accession verified against the resource on 2026-08-18. KEGG modules M00632 and M00061 match two of the nine boundaries exactly; the other seven have no module.
    Effect
    Nine new positive calls become possible. No existing GIFT call changes; the new content shares no reaction with the biosynthetic GIFTs.
Curator noteThe oxidative dehydrogenase route yields different products and is a separate capability. Anchors are declared per GIFT, so the two cannot be routes of one trait.

Change history 2 entries

  1. 2026.09.32026-08-1810:00 UTCbroadens
    Aldose 1-epimerase is optional in the Leloir route
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Mutarotation between the alpha and beta anomers of D-galactose also proceeds spontaneously, so a genome lacking aldose 1-epimerase still runs the Leloir pathway. The reaction is retained at required = 0 so that it appears in the evidence trace without gating the call.
    Evidence
    Spontaneous anomerisation of reducing sugars in aqueous solution; KEGG M00632 includes galM but the pathway operates without it.
    Effect
    Galactose degradation is called in genomes carrying galK, galT and galE but no recognised aldose 1-epimerase.
  2. 2026.09.32026-08-1810:00 UTCbroadens
    Nine monosaccharide and uronate degradation GIFTs added as the first catabolic content
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Monosaccharide catabolism is the tier that connects carbohydrate degradation to central metabolism, and it is the half of the degradation model that needs no polymer chemistry. Each GIFT ends at the central metabolite the sugar actually becomes, so capabilities that yield different products are separate traits rather than routes of one trait.
    Evidence
    Rhea release 141 master reactions and KEGG orthology, every accession verified against the resource on 2026-08-18. KEGG modules M00632 and M00061 match two of the nine boundaries exactly; the other seven have no module.
    Effect
    Nine new positive calls become possible. No existing GIFT call changes; the new content shares no reaction with the biosynthetic GIFTs.
Curator noteBoundaries of KEGG M00632 retained. Aldose 1-epimerase is optional because mutarotation also proceeds spontaneously; UDP-glucose 4-epimerase is required because without it the pathway cannot turn over catalytically.

Change history 1 entry

  1. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCbroadens
    Nine serine, glycine, aspartate-family, cysteine and methionine biosynthesis GIFTs added
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Extend giftr beyond nucleotide metabolism with the amino acid capabilities most often needed to interpret host-associated genomes, curated as bounded capabilities rather than as imported KEGG modules.
    Evidence
    KEGG modules M00016-M00021, M00338 and M00609 for orthology and pathway organisation; Rhea release 141 for reaction identity, direction and ChEBI participants; KEGG gene-to-organism links for the prevalence figures quoted in the accompanying change entries.
    Effect
    Eleven anchors, nine GIFTs, nineteen routes and twenty-five reactions become callable. The amino acid GIFTs compose into a single acyclic chain from 3-phosphoglycerate through serine and cysteine to methionine, and from aspartate through the semialdehyde and homoserine branchpoints to threonine and methionine.
Curator noteNo KEGG module covers this capability. Threonine aldolase is deliberately excluded as a route because it would require L-threonine as an input anchor and adds only 133 KEGG genomes beyond those carrying glyA.

Change history 2 entries

  1. 2026.08.22026-08-1717:45 UTCnone
    Marker layer audited against KEGG orthology; no orthologs missing
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Confirm whether other genomic markers are acceptable for the curated enzymes before broadening the evidence layer, and record the rejected candidates so they are not re-proposed.
    Evidence
    The accepted markers of all 27 reactions were compared against every KO that KEGG assigns to the corresponding EC number, and against the step logic of modules M00048-M00052. Twenty-six of 27 reactions matched exactly; the only difference was the regulatory K00610 retired in this release.
    Effect
    No markers added. K06863 stays off the folate-dependent AICAR transformylase because purP is formate-dependent and modelled as RHEA:24836. K01948 (EC 6.3.4.16) remains unacceptable for the glutamine-dependent RHEA:18633. Non-KO namespaces validate and resolve correctly but were not adopted, because evaluation has no confidence filter and weaker evidence would silently change calls.
  2. 2026.08.12026-08-17none
    Initial curated release of five nucleotide biosynthesis GIFTs
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Establish the reference content of giftr as biologically bounded capabilities between declared molecular anchors, derived from but not equal to KEGG modules M00048 to M00052.
    Evidence
    Rhea release 141 reaction chemistry, ChEBI release 253 anchor identity, KEGG modules M00048-M00052 for pathway organisation and orthology assignment.
    Effect
    Baseline release. Purine core, adenylate, guanylate, pyrimidine core and cytidylate biosynthesis become callable, composing through the shared IMP anchor.
Curator noteAtomic branch derived from KEGG M00050; ends at GMP because shared nucleotide phosphorylation is intentionally excluded.

  1. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCbroadens
    Nine serine, glycine, aspartate-family, cysteine and methionine biosynthesis GIFTs added
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Extend giftr beyond nucleotide metabolism with the amino acid capabilities most often needed to interpret host-associated genomes, curated as bounded capabilities rather than as imported KEGG modules.
    Evidence
    KEGG modules M00016-M00021, M00338 and M00609 for orthology and pathway organisation; Rhea release 141 for reaction identity, direction and ChEBI participants; KEGG gene-to-organism links for the prevalence figures quoted in the accompanying change entries.
    Effect
    Eleven anchors, nine GIFTs, nineteen routes and twenty-five reactions become callable. The amino acid GIFTs compose into a single acyclic chain from 3-phosphoglycerate through serine and cysteine to methionine, and from aspartate through the semialdehyde and homoserine branchpoints to threonine and methionine.
  2. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCnone
    The aspartate-to-homoserine trunk is curated once instead of twice
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    KEGG M00018 and M00017 both contain aspartate kinase, aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase and homoserine dehydrogenase. Importing both modules as GIFTs would encode the same three reactions twice and let the two copies drift apart. The trunk is cut at the two real branchpoints instead.
    Evidence
    6569 KEGG organisms satisfy the orthology of both modules, so the duplication would be exercised in the majority of genomes carrying either. L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde is the branchpoint to lysine and diaminopimelate (M00016); L-homoserine is the branchpoint to threonine and methionine and is named in both module titles.
    Effect
    aspartate_semialdehyde_biosynthesis and homoserine_biosynthesis carry the shared chemistry; threonine and methionine biosynthesis begin at the homoserine anchor and compose through it. The lysine and diaminopimelate branch can later attach at the semialdehyde anchor without re-cutting any existing GIFT.
Curator noteSingle-reaction GIFT shared by KEGG M00018 and M00017. It is not merged into the upstream GIFT because homoserine dehydrogenase is precisely where the lysine branch is left behind.

Change history 4 entries

  1. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCbroadens
    Nine serine, glycine, aspartate-family, cysteine and methionine biosynthesis GIFTs added
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Extend giftr beyond nucleotide metabolism with the amino acid capabilities most often needed to interpret host-associated genomes, curated as bounded capabilities rather than as imported KEGG modules.
    Evidence
    KEGG modules M00016-M00021, M00338 and M00609 for orthology and pathway organisation; Rhea release 141 for reaction identity, direction and ChEBI participants; KEGG gene-to-organism links for the prevalence figures quoted in the accompanying change entries.
    Effect
    Eleven anchors, nine GIFTs, nineteen routes and twenty-five reactions become callable. The amino acid GIFTs compose into a single acyclic chain from 3-phosphoglycerate through serine and cysteine to methionine, and from aspartate through the semialdehyde and homoserine branchpoints to threonine and methionine.
  2. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCnone
    The aspartate-to-homoserine trunk is curated once instead of twice
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    KEGG M00018 and M00017 both contain aspartate kinase, aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase and homoserine dehydrogenase. Importing both modules as GIFTs would encode the same three reactions twice and let the two copies drift apart. The trunk is cut at the two real branchpoints instead.
    Evidence
    6569 KEGG organisms satisfy the orthology of both modules, so the duplication would be exercised in the majority of genomes carrying either. L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde is the branchpoint to lysine and diaminopimelate (M00016); L-homoserine is the branchpoint to threonine and methionine and is named in both module titles.
    Effect
    aspartate_semialdehyde_biosynthesis and homoserine_biosynthesis carry the shared chemistry; threonine and methionine biosynthesis begin at the homoserine anchor and compose through it. The lysine and diaminopimelate branch can later attach at the semialdehyde anchor without re-cutting any existing GIFT.
  3. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCnone
    L-homocysteine is declared as an input anchor only, and methionine biosynthesis is not split at it
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Cysteine to methionine and homocysteine to cysteine is a real metabolic interconversion, so the obvious boundary choices make the anchor-derived composition graph cyclic and the database fails to build. Declaring homocysteine as an output anchor, or curating a methionine-to-homocysteine GIFT, re-creates the cycle.
    Evidence
    The source validator turns every output-anchor to input-anchor match into a directed edge and rejects cycles. With homocysteine as an output the graph closes through METHIONINE, HOMOCYSTEINE and CYSTEINE. In the organisms that use the mcc route the homocysteine consumed by cysteine biosynthesis comes from methionine salvage rather than from de novo methionine biosynthesis, so an input-only boundary is also the honest one.
    Effect
    L-homocysteine stays internal to both methionine GIFTs and is declared only as an input of cysteine_biosynthesis_homocysteine. Any future methionine salvage or SAM-cycle GIFT must revisit this boundary before it can be added.
  4. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCbroadens
    Direct sulfhydrylation added as a methionine biosynthesis capability absent from KEGG M00017
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    M00017 models only transsulfuration, in which cysteine donates the sulfur through cystathionine. Many prokaryotes instead incorporate inorganic sulfide directly into acylated homoserine. Following the module would call those genomes methionine auxotrophs.
    Evidence
    Among KEGG organisms carrying the complete aspartate-to-homoserine trunk and a homoserine acyltransferase, 4096 have only a direct sulfhydrylase, 985 have only the transsulfuration enzymes and 2353 have both. 3910 organisms complete methionine biosynthesis by sulfhydrylation and would be called incomplete by M00017 as written.
    Effect
    methionine_biosynthesis_sulfhydrylation was created with the sulfide input anchor declared. It is kept separate from the transsulfuration capability because anchors are declared per GIFT and not per route, so one GIFT declaring both cysteine and sulfide inputs would over-claim the requirements of both routes.
Curator noteAbsent from KEGG M00017 although 3910 KEGG genomes complete methionine biosynthesis this way and no other. giftr curation, not a KEGG import.
GIFT 22

Homoserine and cysteine to methionine

methionine_biosynthesis_transsulfuration
metabolicamino_acidcuratedv1

Encodes methionine synthesis in which the sulfur is donated by L-cysteine through a cystathionine intermediate, the route used by organisms that assimilate sulfur into cysteine first.

Change history 4 entries

  1. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCbroadens
    Nine serine, glycine, aspartate-family, cysteine and methionine biosynthesis GIFTs added
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Extend giftr beyond nucleotide metabolism with the amino acid capabilities most often needed to interpret host-associated genomes, curated as bounded capabilities rather than as imported KEGG modules.
    Evidence
    KEGG modules M00016-M00021, M00338 and M00609 for orthology and pathway organisation; Rhea release 141 for reaction identity, direction and ChEBI participants; KEGG gene-to-organism links for the prevalence figures quoted in the accompanying change entries.
    Effect
    Eleven anchors, nine GIFTs, nineteen routes and twenty-five reactions become callable. The amino acid GIFTs compose into a single acyclic chain from 3-phosphoglycerate through serine and cysteine to methionine, and from aspartate through the semialdehyde and homoserine branchpoints to threonine and methionine.
  2. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCnone
    The aspartate-to-homoserine trunk is curated once instead of twice
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    KEGG M00018 and M00017 both contain aspartate kinase, aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase and homoserine dehydrogenase. Importing both modules as GIFTs would encode the same three reactions twice and let the two copies drift apart. The trunk is cut at the two real branchpoints instead.
    Evidence
    6569 KEGG organisms satisfy the orthology of both modules, so the duplication would be exercised in the majority of genomes carrying either. L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde is the branchpoint to lysine and diaminopimelate (M00016); L-homoserine is the branchpoint to threonine and methionine and is named in both module titles.
    Effect
    aspartate_semialdehyde_biosynthesis and homoserine_biosynthesis carry the shared chemistry; threonine and methionine biosynthesis begin at the homoserine anchor and compose through it. The lysine and diaminopimelate branch can later attach at the semialdehyde anchor without re-cutting any existing GIFT.
  3. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCnone
    L-homocysteine is declared as an input anchor only, and methionine biosynthesis is not split at it
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Cysteine to methionine and homocysteine to cysteine is a real metabolic interconversion, so the obvious boundary choices make the anchor-derived composition graph cyclic and the database fails to build. Declaring homocysteine as an output anchor, or curating a methionine-to-homocysteine GIFT, re-creates the cycle.
    Evidence
    The source validator turns every output-anchor to input-anchor match into a directed edge and rejects cycles. With homocysteine as an output the graph closes through METHIONINE, HOMOCYSTEINE and CYSTEINE. In the organisms that use the mcc route the homocysteine consumed by cysteine biosynthesis comes from methionine salvage rather than from de novo methionine biosynthesis, so an input-only boundary is also the honest one.
    Effect
    L-homocysteine stays internal to both methionine GIFTs and is declared only as an input of cysteine_biosynthesis_homocysteine. Any future methionine salvage or SAM-cycle GIFT must revisit this boundary before it can be added.
  4. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCbroadens
    Direct sulfhydrylation added as a methionine biosynthesis capability absent from KEGG M00017
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    M00017 models only transsulfuration, in which cysteine donates the sulfur through cystathionine. Many prokaryotes instead incorporate inorganic sulfide directly into acylated homoserine. Following the module would call those genomes methionine auxotrophs.
    Evidence
    Among KEGG organisms carrying the complete aspartate-to-homoserine trunk and a homoserine acyltransferase, 4096 have only a direct sulfhydrylase, 985 have only the transsulfuration enzymes and 2353 have both. 3910 organisms complete methionine biosynthesis by sulfhydrylation and would be called incomplete by M00017 as written.
    Effect
    methionine_biosynthesis_sulfhydrylation was created with the sulfide input anchor declared. It is kept separate from the transsulfuration capability because anchors are declared per GIFT and not per route, so one GIFT declaring both cysteine and sulfide inputs would over-claim the requirements of both routes.
Curator noteTail of KEGG M00017. Separated from the sulfhydrylation capability because the two consume different sulfur substrates, and anchors are declared per GIFT rather than per route. L-homocysteine is deliberately internal here; see database_changes.

Change history 3 entries

  1. 2026.09.42026-08-1814:00 UTCnone
    Uptake GIFTs are curated only where transporter markers are substrate-specific and the translocation has a verified reaction identity
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Fucose, galactose and mannose are moved mainly by promiscuous carriers: the KEGG orthologue for fucose uptake is annotated as a fucose-galactose-glucose symporter, so accepting it would attribute fucose uptake to any genome carrying that family. Sialic acid, hexuronate and N-acetylglucosamine have substrate-specific markers but no reaction identity giftr can verify, because their symporters and importers carry no EC number and no Rhea master. In both cases no uptake GIFT is curated and the substrate anchor stays compartment-unspecified, so no catabolic chain is broken by a transporter that could not be evidenced.
    Evidence
    KEGG orthology entry K02429, annotated as an MFS fucose-galactose-glucose:H+ symporter; absence of an EC number or Rhea master for K03290 (nanT), K08191 (exuT) and K10200/K10201/K10202 (ngcEFG).
    Effect
    No call changes. Seven substrates keep an unspecified anchor and remain callable from their catabolic markers alone.
  2. 2026.09.32026-08-1810:00 UTCnarrows
    The bifunctional biosynthetic enzyme GNE is not accepted as evidence for N-acetylmannosamine kinase
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    GNE (K12409) carries a N-acetylmannosamine kinase domain and so catalyses the curated chemistry, but in the organisms that encode it that activity belongs to sialic acid biosynthesis rather than catabolism. Accepting it would call sialic acid degradation in genomes that only synthesise it, destroying the distinction the GIFT exists to draw.
    Evidence
    KEGG orthology entry K12409, annotated as bifunctional UDP-N-acetylglucosamine 2-epimerase / N-acetylmannosamine kinase.
    Effect
    N-acetylneuraminate degradation is not called from GNE alone. Genomes carrying nanK or the bifunctional nanEK are unaffected.
  3. 2026.09.32026-08-1810:00 UTCbroadens
    Nine monosaccharide and uronate degradation GIFTs added as the first catabolic content
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Monosaccharide catabolism is the tier that connects carbohydrate degradation to central metabolism, and it is the half of the degradation model that needs no polymer chemistry. Each GIFT ends at the central metabolite the sugar actually becomes, so capabilities that yield different products are separate traits rather than routes of one trait.
    Evidence
    Rhea release 141 master reactions and KEGG orthology, every accession verified against the resource on 2026-08-18. KEGG modules M00632 and M00061 match two of the nine boundaries exactly; the other seven have no module.
    Effect
    Nine new positive calls become possible. No existing GIFT call changes; the new content shares no reaction with the biosynthetic GIFTs.
Curator noteShares the deacetylase and deaminase reactions with GlcNAc degradation but is not a composite of it: the shared intermediate is N-acetyl-D-glucosamine 6-phosphate, which is internal to both and is deliberately not an anchor.

Change history 1 entry

  1. 2026.12.32026-08-1811:20 UTCbroadens
    Phosphate starvation response added with two cognate-pair circuits
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The regulatory proposal recorded orthology calibration as the question blocking this trait: whether K07636 and K07657 distinguish a cognate Pho pair from a genome full of paralogous kinases and regulators. The calibration was done and the answer separated one capability into two circuits sharing a sensor.
    Evidence
    Gene counts per genome from the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18. K07636 is single-copy in Escherichia coli, Bacillus subtilis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Salmonella Typhi and Vibrio cholerae, and absent from Campylobacter jejuni, Helicobacter pylori, Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Lactococcus lactis. K07657 is single-copy in the four Gram-negatives and absent from Bacillus subtilis, which instead carries K07658 at BSU29110, immediately adjacent to the K07636 sensor BSU29100. The two regulator groups are mutually exclusive across the genomes checked.
    Effect
    phosphate_starvation_response becomes callable through CIRCUIT_PHO_PHOR_PHOB and CIRCUIT_PHO_PHOR_PHOP, which share the RF_PHO_SIGNAL_RECEPTION function. K07660, the response regulator of the magnesium-sensing PhoP/PhoQ system, is refused despite sharing the gene name. PstSCAB-PhoU is accessory.
Curator noteTwo curated circuits share the PhoR sensor and differ in the response regulator: PhoB (K07657) in enterobacteria, pseudomonads and vibrios, PhoP (K07658) in Bacillus and relatives. Across the reference genomes checked on 2026-08-18 the sensor is single-copy where present and the two regulator groups are mutually exclusive, which is what licenses orthology as evidence of a cognate pair here. K07660, the response regulator of the magnesium-sensing PhoP/PhoQ system, shares the gene name and is a different protein; it is not accepted. The PstSCAB-PhoU complex is accessory because it is independently a transport capability.

Change history 2 entries

  1. 2026.08.22026-08-1717:45 UTCnone
    Marker layer audited against KEGG orthology; no orthologs missing
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Confirm whether other genomic markers are acceptable for the curated enzymes before broadening the evidence layer, and record the rejected candidates so they are not re-proposed.
    Evidence
    The accepted markers of all 27 reactions were compared against every KO that KEGG assigns to the corresponding EC number, and against the step logic of modules M00048-M00052. Twenty-six of 27 reactions matched exactly; the only difference was the regulatory K00610 retired in this release.
    Effect
    No markers added. K06863 stays off the folate-dependent AICAR transformylase because purP is formate-dependent and modelled as RHEA:24836. K01948 (EC 6.3.4.16) remains unacceptable for the glutamine-dependent RHEA:18633. Non-KO namespaces validate and resolve correctly but were not adopted, because evaluation has no confidence filter and weaker evidence would silently change calls.
  2. 2026.08.12026-08-17none
    Initial curated release of five nucleotide biosynthesis GIFTs
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Establish the reference content of giftr as biologically bounded capabilities between declared molecular anchors, derived from but not equal to KEGG modules M00048 to M00052.
    Evidence
    Rhea release 141 reaction chemistry, ChEBI release 253 anchor identity, KEGG modules M00048-M00052 for pathway organisation and orthology assignment.
    Effect
    Baseline release. Purine core, adenylate, guanylate, pyrimidine core and cytidylate biosynthesis become callable, composing through the shared IMP anchor.

Change history 4 entries

  1. 2026.08.22026-08-1717:45 UTCbroadens
    Aspartate carbamoyltransferase no longer requires the PyrI regulatory subunit
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    PyrI is an allosteric regulator, not a catalytic subunit, and class C aspartate carbamoyltransferases are catalytic trimers with no regulatory subunit. Requiring K00610 asserted a subunit that most prokaryotes do not encode. The previous definition followed the KEGG module expression (K00609+K00610,K00608), which is a pathway drawing convention rather than an evidence claim.
    Evidence
    Of 9670 KEGG organisms carrying K00609, 7863 carry neither K00610 nor K00608. Bacillus subtilis, Lactococcus lactis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus and Mycobacterium tuberculosis, all de novo pyrimidine prototrophs, were called incomplete at RHEA:20013 when evaluated from their complete KEGG orthology annotation.
    Effect
    SYS_20013_HOLOENZYME became the single-component SYS_20013_CATALYTIC, satisfied by K00609 alone; COMP_20013_REGULATORY and marker K00610 were removed. Those five reference genomes now complete the GIFT; no genome lost a previously complete call.
  2. 2026.08.22026-08-1717:45 UTCnarrows
    NAD-dependent dihydroorotate oxidation now requires the PyrK electron transfer subunit
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The class 1B enzyme is a PyrDb/PyrK holoenzyme. The catalytic subunit alone cannot reduce NAD+, so accepting K17828 by itself claimed the NAD-dependent chemistry from half of the enzyme. KEGG module M00051 lists only K17828 for this step.
    Evidence
    KEGG annotates K02823 (pyrDII/PyrK) to the same reaction R01869 as K17828, and 2403 of the 2724 organisms carrying K17828 also carry K02823.
    Effect
    SYS_13513_NAD gained the required component COMP_13513_ELECTRON accepting K02823. Genomes annotated with K17828 but not K02823 now report RHEA:13513 as unsupported and fall back to the fumarate-dependent or quinone-dependent route. None of the nine reference genomes changed.
  3. 2026.08.22026-08-1717:45 UTCnone
    Marker layer audited against KEGG orthology; no orthologs missing
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Confirm whether other genomic markers are acceptable for the curated enzymes before broadening the evidence layer, and record the rejected candidates so they are not re-proposed.
    Evidence
    The accepted markers of all 27 reactions were compared against every KO that KEGG assigns to the corresponding EC number, and against the step logic of modules M00048-M00052. Twenty-six of 27 reactions matched exactly; the only difference was the regulatory K00610 retired in this release.
    Effect
    No markers added. K06863 stays off the folate-dependent AICAR transformylase because purP is formate-dependent and modelled as RHEA:24836. K01948 (EC 6.3.4.16) remains unacceptable for the glutamine-dependent RHEA:18633. Non-KO namespaces validate and resolve correctly but were not adopted, because evaluation has no confidence filter and weaker evidence would silently change calls.
  4. 2026.08.12026-08-17none
    Initial curated release of five nucleotide biosynthesis GIFTs
    Why, evidence and effect

Change history 1 entry

  1. 2026.09.32026-08-1810:00 UTCbroadens
    Nine monosaccharide and uronate degradation GIFTs added as the first catabolic content
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Monosaccharide catabolism is the tier that connects carbohydrate degradation to central metabolism, and it is the half of the degradation model that needs no polymer chemistry. Each GIFT ends at the central metabolite the sugar actually becomes, so capabilities that yield different products are separate traits rather than routes of one trait.
    Evidence
    Rhea release 141 master reactions and KEGG orthology, every accession verified against the resource on 2026-08-18. KEGG modules M00632 and M00061 match two of the nine boundaries exactly; the other seven have no module.
    Effect
    Nine new positive calls become possible. No existing GIFT call changes; the new content shares no reaction with the biosynthetic GIFTs.
Curator noteShares product anchors with fucose degradation but no reactions; the two isomerase, kinase and aldolase families are non-homologous.

    Nine serine, glycine, aspartate-family, cysteine and methionine biosynthesis GIFTs added
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Extend giftr beyond nucleotide metabolism with the amino acid capabilities most often needed to interpret host-associated genomes, curated as bounded capabilities rather than as imported KEGG modules.
    Evidence
    KEGG modules M00016-M00021, M00338 and M00609 for orthology and pathway organisation; Rhea release 141 for reaction identity, direction and ChEBI participants; KEGG gene-to-organism links for the prevalence figures quoted in the accompanying change entries.
    Effect
    Eleven anchors, nine GIFTs, nineteen routes and twenty-five reactions become callable. The amino acid GIFTs compose into a single acyclic chain from 3-phosphoglycerate through serine and cysteine to methionine, and from aspartate through the semialdehyde and homoserine branchpoints to threonine and methionine.
Curator noteBoundaries of KEGG M00020 retained. The phosphoserine phosphatase step is kept required even though a fifth of serA/serC genomes carry no recognised phosphatase orthologue; the chemistry is required and the missing reaction is reported rather than silently scored away.

Change history 7 entries

  1. 2026.11.12026-08-1823:59 UTCbroadens
    CAZy subfamily markers curated from the dbCAN-sub HMM library, with confidence from measured EC dominance
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Marker policy prefers a subfamily over a polyspecific family, but the family-level substrate mapping shipped by dbCAN contains no subfamily rows, so the first polysaccharide release accepted bare families and recorded them as ambiguous. The subfamily assignments live in the dbCAN-sub HMM library, whose profile names encode the eCAMI cluster, its parent family, the official CAZy subfamilies it contains, and the EC numbers its members carry, each with a member count. Streaming the library and keeping only those names yields a 104 KB table from a 4.9 GB artifact. Confidence now comes from two measured quantities rather than one: how dominant an EC is among the EC-annotated members of a cluster, and how many members support it. Clusters whose parent family belongs to a different catalytic class are excluded, and carbohydrate-binding modules are excluded entirely because they catalyse nothing.
    Evidence
    dbCAN-sub HMM library db_v5-2-9_5-5-2026, 53411 profiles, of which 2474 carry at least one EC assignment; derived table in data-raw/reference/cazy-subfamily-ec.tsv with the extraction script alongside it.
    Effect
    267 subfamily evidence rows added across seven catalytic components. Genomes annotated by dbCAN-sub gain calls they previously missed, and a call resting on a specific subfamily now reports curated or high-confidence where a bare family reported ambiguous. Bare families are retained as a lower-confidence fallback, so no genome loses a call.
  2. 2026.11.12026-08-1823:59 UTCnone
    GIFTs and anchors carry a registered facet vocabulary, and a derived profile is exposed alongside it
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    A single free-text category could not answer questions that cut across it, and the information needed to answer them was already present in the declared anchors and the compartment layer with no way out. The facet vocabulary is registered so that a multi-valued classification cannot degenerate into free text: substrate_class is single-valued and therefore partitions the database, while physiological_role and the anchor facets are multi-valued and return supersets. Nothing in the derived profile is curated, and neither facets nor profile enter the completeness logic that produces a call.
    Evidence
    Declared anchors, anchor compartment, and the anchor-derived composition graph, all already present in the database.
    Effect
    No call changes. The former gift.category column is replaced by the substrate_class facet.
  3. 2026.10.32026-08-1823:00 UTCnone
    The curator note for polymer saccharification no longer claims that the exo-acting enzyme cannot release a monosaccharide on its own
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The note justified requiring both activities by asserting that neither alone liberates a usable monosaccharide. The second half of that is chemically wrong. EC 3.2.1.37 is defined by IUBMB as xylan 1,4-beta-xylosidase, removing successive D-xylose residues from the non-reducing termini of xylans, so it can release D-xylose from the polymer directly; the same applies to EC 3.2.1.20 on alpha-glucan termini. The reason both reactions are required is a curation decision about what counts as evidence for effective polymer-to-monosaccharide saccharification, not a claim about what either enzyme can catalyse. Endo-acting cleavage generates the additional chain ends that make exo-acting release productive on a polymer rather than marginal.
    Evidence
    IUBMB enzyme nomenclature for EC 3.2.1.37 and EC 3.2.1.20; the curated reaction description of RXN_XYLOOLIGO_EXO already stated the correct substrate.
    Effect
    No call changes and no route changes. The requirement is unaltered; only its stated justification is corrected.
  4. 2026.10.22026-08-1821:00 UTCmixed
    Polysaccharide degradation is curated per substrate capability rather than per enzymatic step
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The first polysaccharide release split each substrate into single-reaction GIFTs for endo-acting depolymerisation, exo-acting saccharification and debranching. That made a GIFT equivalent to a reaction, which is the marker-checklist shape the ontology exists to avoid, and it left the question a user actually asks - can this genome degrade xylan - unanswerable by any single trait. The separation was motivated by the primary-degrader versus cross-feeder distinction, which is real, but that distinction is already carried by the incomplete-route diagnostics: a genome with only the endo-acting enzyme is now reported as incomplete with the exo-acting reaction named as missing, which is more informative than a separate positive trait because it says what is absent. Oligosaccharide intermediates return to being internal; they would be promoted back to anchors only if an oligosaccharide importer could be evidenced, which would make selfish foraging an independently meaningful capability.
    Evidence
    giftr evaluation contract: route completeness with closest-route and missing-reaction reporting. Invariant 9 of AGENTS.md, which forbids both arbitrary single-step fragments and bundles of independently meaningful capabilities.
    Effect
    Six single-reaction GIFTs are replaced by three substrate-level capabilities. Genomes carrying a complete endo-plus-exo enzyme set keep a positive call; genomes carrying only one side of it now report an incomplete capability with the missing reaction named, where they previously reported a positive call for a fragment. Two anchors are withdrawn.
  5. 2026.10.12026-08-1818:00 UTCnone
    CAZy families accepted as markers, with confidence derived from measured family polyspecificity
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    A CAZy family is a sequence family, not an activity. Accepting a family as evidence for one of its activities silently attributes the others, so confidence is set from the number of distinct characterised activities the family carries in dbCAN: one activity is curated, two or three is high-confidence, four or more is ambiguous. GH5 carries 28 and GH13 carries 34, so neither is evidence for a specific chemistry on its own; GH52, GH120 and GH62 carry one each.
    Evidence
    Distinct EC counts computed directly from the pinned dbCAN mapping and recorded per marker in component_markers.notes.
    Effect
    Calls resting only on polyspecific families report evidence_confidence = ambiguous rather than reading like curated orthology.
  6. 2026.10.12026-08-1818:00 UTCnone
    A CAZy family and a KEGG orthologue are alternative markers of one catalytic role, not alternative enzyme systems
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    The proposal suggested one enzyme system per non-homologous CAZy family. At implementation these are all single-protein hydrolases, and an annotation pipeline cannot tell whether the family hit and the orthology hit describe the same protein - they usually do. Modelling them as alternative systems would imply two enzymes where there is one. The system and component layers remain available for genuinely multi-subunit CAZyme architectures.
    Evidence
    Absence of subunit structure in the curated hydrolases; overlap between CAZy and KEGG annotation of the same protein.
    Effect
    No call changes; the Boolean result is identical either way.
  7. 2026.10.12026-08-1818:00 UTCbroadens
    Arabinoxylan and starch depolymerisation and saccharification curated as separate tiers
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Endo-acting depolymerisation and exo-acting saccharification are curated as separate GIFTs because possessing one without the other is the primary-degrader versus cross-feeder distinction, which is the main thing a carbohydrate database is asked to resolve. Polymer and oligosaccharide anchors are extracellular: a polymer cannot cross a membrane, and no oligosaccharide importer could be evidenced, so the products of their cleavage are outside the cell. Side-chain release earns its own GIFT because the released L-arabinose is itself an anchored fermentable sugar.
    Evidence
    CAZy family and activity assignments from dbCAN db_v5-2-9_5-5-2026 fam-substrate-mapping.tsv; KEGG orthology entries verified 2026-08-18. None of the six EC numbers has a Rhea master reaction.
    Effect
    Six new positive calls become possible, and the first complete traversal from a dietary polysaccharide to central metabolism appears in the derived graph.
Curator noteEndo- and exo-acting chemistry are both required for this curated saccharification capability. Alpha-amylase depolymerises the alpha-1,4-glucan backbone and generates additional chain ends and malto-oligosaccharides, while alpha-glucosidase releases D-glucose successively from non-reducing termini. As for xylan, the exo-acting enzyme can in principle act on polymer termini directly, but exo activity alone is not treated here as sufficient evidence for complete polymer saccharification. Debranching is accessory rather than required: amylose carries no alpha-1,6 branch points, so a genome without pullulanase still degrades starch, less completely. Malto-oligosaccharide is an internal intermediate for the same reason as xylo-oligosaccharide.

Change history 2 entries

  1. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCbroadens
    Nine serine, glycine, aspartate-family, cysteine and methionine biosynthesis GIFTs added
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    Extend giftr beyond nucleotide metabolism with the amino acid capabilities most often needed to interpret host-associated genomes, curated as bounded capabilities rather than as imported KEGG modules.
    Evidence
    KEGG modules M00016-M00021, M00338 and M00609 for orthology and pathway organisation; Rhea release 141 for reaction identity, direction and ChEBI participants; KEGG gene-to-organism links for the prevalence figures quoted in the accompanying change entries.
    Effect
    Eleven anchors, nine GIFTs, nineteen routes and twenty-five reactions become callable. The amino acid GIFTs compose into a single acyclic chain from 3-phosphoglycerate through serine and cysteine to methionine, and from aspartate through the semialdehyde and homoserine branchpoints to threonine and methionine.
  2. 2026.09.12026-08-1720:10 UTCnone
    The aspartate-to-homoserine trunk is curated once instead of twice
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    KEGG M00018 and M00017 both contain aspartate kinase, aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase and homoserine dehydrogenase. Importing both modules as GIFTs would encode the same three reactions twice and let the two copies drift apart. The trunk is cut at the two real branchpoints instead.
    Evidence
    6569 KEGG organisms satisfy the orthology of both modules, so the duplication would be exercised in the majority of genomes carrying either. L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde is the branchpoint to lysine and diaminopimelate (M00016); L-homoserine is the branchpoint to threonine and methionine and is named in both module titles.
    Effect
    aspartate_semialdehyde_biosynthesis and homoserine_biosynthesis carry the shared chemistry; threonine and methionine biosynthesis begin at the homoserine anchor and compose through it. The lysine and diaminopimelate branch can later attach at the semialdehyde anchor without re-cutting any existing GIFT.
Curator noteTail of KEGG M00018; the aspartate-to-homoserine head is curated separately and composed through the homoserine anchor.
GIFT 31

Type I-E CRISPR-Cas machinery

type_i_e_crispr_cas_machinery
defense—curatedv1

Encodes the protein machinery of a type I-E CRISPR-Cas system: the five-subunit Cascade surveillance complex and the Cas3 nuclease-helicase, with Cas1-Cas2 spacer acquisition accessory. A positive call means the genome encodes those proteins. It does not mean the system can interfere with anything, because interference additionally requires a CRISPR array to supply guide RNAs, and an array is a repeat-spacer locus detected by structure rather than a protein annotation.

Change history 1 entry

  1. 2026.12.32026-08-1811:40 UTCbroadens
    Type I-E CRISPR-Cas curated as an encoded-machinery claim, not an interference claim
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    A CRISPR-Cas system without a CRISPR array has no guide RNAs and interferes with nothing, and an array is a repeat-spacer locus detected by structure rather than a protein annotation. giftr's evidence layer is a namespaced accession and cannot express it. Rather than pretend protein markers cover the array, or refuse the trait entirely, the claim was narrowed to what the evidence supports.
    Evidence
    KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18: K19123, K19046, K19124, K19125 and K19126 are defined as Cascade subunits CasA, CasB, CasC, CasD and CasE, and K07012 as the Cas3 endonuclease-helicase. Escherichia coli K-12 carries one of each plus K15342 and K09951.
    Effect
    type_i_e_crispr_cas_machinery becomes callable through MECH_TYPE_I_E_CRISPR with Cascade and Cas3 required and Cas1-Cas2 adaptation accessory. The array limitation is stated in the GIFT description rather than a footnote. K07475, the HD module of a split Cas3, is refused as evidence of the complete nuclease-helicase. Extending the evidence model to genomic features is deferred to a second demonstrated need.
Curator noteThe claim is deliberately narrowed to the encoded machinery. giftr's evidence layer is an annotation accession, which cannot express 'a CRISPR array was detected in this genome', and no Cas protein accession is evidence that an array is present. Broadening the evidence model to genomic features was considered and deferred to a second demonstrated need; see inst/doc/proposal-defense-gifts.md.
GIFT 32

Type I restriction-modification

type_i_restriction_modification
defense—curatedv1

Encodes a complete type I restriction-modification system: the HsdS specificity subunit, the HsdM methyltransferase that protects the host's own target sites, and the HsdR subunit that translocates and cleaves unmethylated DNA. A positive call means the genome encodes that mechanism. It does not mean the organism resists any particular phage, which depends on the invader's anti-restriction counter-measures and on defences this GIFT does not describe.

Change history 1 entry

  1. 2026.12.32026-08-1811:30 UTCbroadens
    Type I restriction-modification added as the first defense GIFT
    Why, evidence and effect
    Rationale
    A defense capability is not the sum of its convenient parts. Type I restriction-modification was curated first because it makes that explicit: the mechanism is complete only when recognition, host protection and restriction are all encoded, and the multisubunit requirement is real rather than a modelling choice.
    Evidence
    KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18. K01153, K03427 and K01154 are defined as the R, M and S subunits of a type I restriction enzyme, so the accessions separate type I from types II, III and IV. Escherichia coli K-12 carries one of each, the EcoKI system.
    Effect
    type_i_restriction_modification becomes callable through MECH_TYPE_I_RM with three required functions. A genome carrying only HsdM and HsdS is called incomplete, missing DF_TYPE_I_RM_RESTRICTION. The target sequence recognised by HsdS is not claimed, because the variable target recognition domains are not resolved by the orthology group.
Curator noteAll three subunits are required. A genome carrying only HsdM and HsdS has a methylation capability, which is real biology and common as an orphan methyltransferase, but it defends against nothing and is correctly called incomplete here. The target sequence the system recognises is deliberately not claimed: HsdS specificity comes from variable target recognition domains that the orthology group does not resolve.
