Receptor distribution was measured rather than assumed: Escherichia coli K-12 carries no K03406 orthologue, its four receptors being assigned to the characterised groups K05874, K05875, K05876 and K03776, while Pseudomonas aeruginosa carries 21 K03406 genes and Vibrio cholerae 34.chemotaxis_signal_transduction becomes callable through CIRCUIT_CHEMOTAXIS_CORE with four required functions. The reception function accepts a generic or a characterised chemoreceptor, so an Escherichia coli annotation is not called receptor-less. Signal termination is accessory with three non-homologous systems.
35DBC-20260818-CHEMOTAXIS-SPECIFICITY2026.12.32026-08-18T11:10Zregulatory_componentadditionnarrowsLigand-specific chemoreception curated as a separate claim with separate evidenceRegulatory specificity cannot exceed evidence specificity. A generic methyl-accepting chemotaxis protein identifies the conserved cytoplasmic signalling domain shared by every chemoreceptor and says nothing about the periplasmic domain that determines what is detected. Rather than leave the principle implicit, a narrower claim was curated with strictly narrower evidence.K03406 is assigned to 34 genes in Vibrio cholerae and 21 in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, so it cannot single out any one chemoeffector. K05875 is the Tar orthologue group, anchored on the characterised aspartate and maltose sensor of Escherichia coli and Salmonella.aspartate_chemoreception requires K05875 for its reception function and refuses K03406. A genome carrying only a generic chemoreceptor completes chemotaxis_signal_transduction and not aspartate_chemoreception, which is the intended behaviour.
36DBC-20260818-PHO-TWO-CIRCUITS2026.12.32026-08-18T11:20ZgiftadditionbroadensPhosphate starvation response added with two cognate-pair circuitsThe regulatory proposal recorded orthology calibration as the question blocking this trait: whether K07636 and K07657 distinguish a cognate Pho pair from a genome full of paralogous kinases and regulators. The calibration was done and the answer separated one capability into two circuits sharing a sensor.Gene counts per genome from the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18. K07636 is single-copy in Escherichia coli, Bacillus subtilis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Salmonella Typhi and Vibrio cholerae, and absent from Campylobacter jejuni, Helicobacter pylori, Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Lactococcus lactis. K07657 is single-copy in the four Gram-negatives and absent from Bacillus subtilis, which instead carries K07658 at BSU29110, immediately adjacent to the K07636 sensor BSU29100. The two regulator groups are mutually exclusive across the genomes checked.phosphate_starvation_response becomes callable through CIRCUIT_PHO_PHOR_PHOB and CIRCUIT_PHO_PHOR_PHOP, which share the RF_PHO_SIGNAL_RECEPTION function. K07660, the response regulator of the magnesium-sensing PhoP/PhoQ system, is refused despite sharing the gene name. PstSCAB-PhoU is accessory.
37DBC-20260818-TYPE-I-RM2026.12.32026-08-18T11:30ZgiftadditionbroadensType I restriction-modification added as the first defense GIFTA defense capability is not the sum of its convenient parts. Type I restriction-modification was curated first because it makes that explicit: the mechanism is complete only when recognition, host protection and restriction are all encoded, and the multisubunit requirement is real rather than a modelling choice.KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18. K01153, K03427 and K01154 are defined as the R, M and S subunits of a type I restriction enzyme, so the accessions separate type I from types II, III and IV. Escherichia coli K-12 carries one of each, the EcoKI system.type_i_restriction_modification becomes callable through MECH_TYPE_I_RM with three required functions. A genome carrying only HsdM and HsdS is called incomplete, missing DF_TYPE_I_RM_RESTRICTION. The target sequence recognised by HsdS is not claimed, because the variable target recognition domains are not resolved by the orthology group.
38DBC-20260818-CRISPR-ARRAY-LIMIT2026.12.32026-08-18T11:40ZgiftadditionbroadensType I-E CRISPR-Cas curated as an encoded-machinery claim, not an interference claimA CRISPR-Cas system without a CRISPR array has no guide RNAs and interferes with nothing, and an array is a repeat-spacer locus detected by structure rather than a protein annotation. giftr's evidence layer is a namespaced accession and cannot express it. Rather than pretend protein markers cover the array, or refuse the trait entirely, the claim was narrowed to what the evidence supports.KEGG orthology, verified against the KEGG REST API on 2026-08-18: K19123, K19046, K19124, K19125 and K19126 are defined as Cascade subunits CasA, CasB, CasC, CasD and CasE, and K07012 as the Cas3 endonuclease-helicase. Escherichia coli K-12 carries one of each plus K15342 and K09951.type_i_e_crispr_cas_machinery becomes callable through MECH_TYPE_I_E_CRISPR with Cascade and Cas3 required and Cas1-Cas2 adaptation accessory. The array limitation is stated in the GIFT description rather than a footnote. K07475, the HD module of a split Cas3, is refused as evidence of the complete nuclease-helicase. Extending the evidence model to genomic features is deferred to a second demonstrated need.
